notes: v4.2/v4.3 upstream-clone debugging task on the real libvips tree (libvips/libvips issue #4877, fix 7cfd70a869de8fe3f3a22b32f755e382130b716c; parent ea7e608844b85f4d296821e59b2483369b301b53; the mining entry guessed 'easy', the measured family rubric lands at 13, medium). The image carries a shallow clone pinned to the parent commit, already built with meson/ninja and installed system-wide, with pyvips==3.2.0 + pytest==8.4.2 bound to it, so the agent's work is: reproduce (a pyvips reproducer shipped as /app/reproduce.py shows out-of-bounds draw_flood start points being silently accepted), localise, add the missing start-point bounds check in libvips/draw/draw_flood.c, and redo only `ninja -C build install`. The upstream fix commit is deliberately unreachable from the clone (shallow fetch pins only the parent; the golden fix-era test_draw.py is extracted into /opt/golden from a throwaway clone whose sha256 is pinned in the Dockerfile, and the verifier asserts `git cat-file -e <fix>` fails). The Dockerfile liveness gate fails closed: the reproducer must report the bug and the golden regression must FAIL at the parent build; the installed parent .so must lack the fix string. The verifier runs the project's own draw suite (fix-era test_draw.py = parent suite + regression assertion, overlaid at verify time), requires the working tree to be otherwise unmodified vs baseline (only draw_flood.c), requires the INSTALLED .so to contain the bounds-check message (closes the fix-pyvips-instead loophole), and adds 3 authored hidden cases: (1) a 640x480 image with starts exactly on the right/bottom boundary and one pixel past the corner plus a valid bottom-right-corner fill; (2) draw_flood1 with far offsets (1000) and exact-boundary offsets plus an all-pixels full-fill expectation; (3) an explicit test-image annulus flood whose filled set is computed in pure Python (ring pixels painted, hole/outside untouched) plus an OOB start with the test image bound. All three hidden cases fail on the buggy parent build and pass on the fixed build. The nop container scores 0: reproducer and suite fail, no diagnosis exists, and the installed .so lacks the fix string. Both directions were re-confirmed inside the built task image (observed outputs reported). Offline-clean: nothing at trial time fetches from the network; ninja rebuild, ldconfig, pytest, pyvips all run with no network, and parent/fix builds share soname libvips.so.42.20.0 so no stale-.so shadowing can occur. REVIEW (2026-09-12): tightens — (1) the verifier snapshots the installed Python binding tree (pyvips + cffi + the abi extension) at build time into /opt/python-site.sha256 and fails if it changes or if new site-packages files appear, closing the monkeypatch-the-binding loophole (proven exploitable: dead string in draw_flood.c + pyvips wrapper scored 1 on the unpatched verifier and scores 0 now); (2) the verifier re-verifies /opt/golden/test_draw.py against the pinned fix-era upstream sha256; (3) hidden case 4 added: a ctypes-level check that drives vips_draw_flood1 directly (immune to Python-layer patches; fails at parent, passes at fix). Both acceptance directions re-verified: oracle 1, nop 0.
